Every 2025 required minimum distribution was taken in full, from the right accounts, well before the 1 April 2026 deadline. The amounts taken match what I calculated to the cent.

**Who owed one.** Only Prema has retirement accounts: two traditional IRAs (SYN-58140002 and SYN-58140003) and her former employer's 401(k) (SYN-58140004). Martin is the named beneficiary but owns no retirement accounts. Prema was born 22 July 1952 and turned 73 in 2025. That made 2025 her first distribution year, so the deadline was 1 April 2026. She retired from the 401(k) employer in 2020, so the plan's still-working exception doesn't apply.

**Factor.** Martin is less than 10 years younger than Prema, so the IRS Uniform Lifetime Table applies. Its factor at age 73 is 26.5.

**Amounts.** Each account's value on 31 Dec 2024 is its holdings plus cash, divided by 26.5:

| Account | 31 Dec 2024 value | 2025 RMD |
|---|---|---|
| SYN-58140002 IRA | 279,796.55 + 74,838.64 + 214,811.75 + 13,000.00 = **582,446.94** | **21,979.13** |
| SYN-58140003 IRA | 109,797.44 + 79,978.32 + 5,000.00 = **194,775.76** | **7,350.03** |
| SYN-58140004 401(k) | 174,976.00 + 129,981.24 + 7,000.00 = **311,957.24** | **11,771.97** |

**What was taken.**
- **IRAs:** IRA required minimums can be added together and taken from either IRA. Together these two came to $29,329.16. On 4 Dec 2025 that exact gross amount was paid from SYN-58140002, matching the instruction Prema signed on 24 Nov 2025 and that account's 1099-R (Box 1 $29,329.16, $2,932.92 withheld).
- **401(k):** A 401(k)'s required minimum can't be combined with IRAs; it has to come from the plan itself. On 5 Nov 2025 the plan paid out exactly $11,771.97 gross, matching the 1099-R (Box 1 $11,771.97, $1,177.20 withheld).

No other retirement distributions or rollovers appear in 2025 or 2026 up to the deadline.
